mainTopic: What a buyer of a dovecote's, beehive's or tree's yearly produce must leave for the seller, and whether honey in a hive counts as food
overview: The משנה lists four sales where the buyer gets only the yearly output and must leave something for the seller: the first brood of a dovecote, bees beyond three swarms, two honeycombs, and two olive shoots. The גמרא asks why a ברייתא says two broods are left. רב כהנא answers that one pair keeps the mother dove and one keeps the daughter, because a mother clings to her daughter but a daughter does not cling to her mother. Next, the גמרא asks how the bees are made sterile. שמואל says it is done with mustard, and the scholars of ארץ ישראל explain that the mustard makes the bees eat their own honey, and that is what stops them from swarming. רבי יוחנן reads the משנה's word differently: the buyer takes three swarms by skipping every other one. A ברייתא gives a third way: three swarms in a row, and then one for the buyer and one for the seller. Finally, רב כהנא rules that honey in a hive is always food for טומאה. A ברייתא seems to say the opposite. אביי limits that ברייתא to the two combs left for the bees, and רבא says it follows רבי אליעזר; his explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה: what a buyer must leave for the seller
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that someone buying the yearly output of a dovecote, beehive, honeycombs or olive trees must leave a little behind so the seller's source keeps going.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you buy the doves a dovecote will produce, you leave the first brood. If you buy what a beehive produces, you take three swarms and then the bees are made sterile. If you buy honeycombs, you leave two combs. If you buy olive trees to cut down, you leave two shoots.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives four cases of buying 'produce' and says what the buyer must leave for the seller in each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer only bought what the source yields, not the source itself. So he must leave enough behind for the dovecote, hive, comb or tree to keep producing for the seller. Each case has its own amount.

keyTerms.meaning: Dovecote, a house where doves live and breed
A brood, the young doves hatched at one time
Literally 'lets fly'; here, he leaves it alone for the seller
Makes sterile, so they stop breeding
Shoots that grow back from a cut tree

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the base text for the whole סוגיא. Each question in the גמרא below works through one of these rulings.

phrases.english: MISHNA
One who buys the produce of a dovecote from his fellow
lets the first brood go free.
phrases.notes: He means the buyer doesn't take the first pair of chicks; they stay with the seller.

phrases.english: The produce of a beehive:
he takes three swarms, and then makes them sterile.
Honeycombs: he leaves two combs.
Olive trees for cutting down:
he leaves two shoots.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A buyer of a source's yearly produce must leave part of it for the seller: the first brood, everything beyond three swarms, two combs, and two shoots.

steps.title: A ברייתא says two broods are left, not one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה with a ברייתא that says the first AND second broods are left for the seller.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: the first brood and the second brood!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that a ברייתא seems to argue with the משנה about how many broods the buyer leaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה mentions only the first brood. The ברייתא adds the second brood too. Either the sources disagree, or they need to be explained.

phrases.english: GEMARA
But isn't it taught in a baraita:
the first and the second brood!

steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that only the first brood is left
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא requires leaving two broods, which contradicts the משנה's one.

steps.title: One pair for the daughter, one for the mother
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא says both sources are right: one pair is left for the brood itself, and the ברייתא also counts a pair left for the mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: No problem. This one is for her, and that one is for her mother.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא settles the contradiction by saying the two sources are counting different pairs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה speaks of the pair left so the young dove (the 'daughter') stays. The ברייתא also counts the pair left for the mother dove. So the ברייתא's two broods include the משנה's one. They don't argue.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is not difficult', which opens an answer
'This ... that', splitting the two sources into two cases

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said: It is not difficult;
this is for her, and that is for her mother.
phrases.notes: 'Her' is the young dove from the first brood; 'her mother' is the older dove that hatched her.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (הָא בְּ... הָא בְּ...)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and ברייתא disagree about how many broods are left.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה speaks of the pair left for the daughter; the ברייתא also counts the pair left for the mother.

steps.title: Why can't the daughter stay because of her mother?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the mother stays because she is attached to her daughter and mate, the daughter should also stay because of her mother and mate. Why leave an extra pair for her?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about the mother? She stays because she is attached to her daughter and the mate we leave for her. The daughter too should be attached to her mother and the mate we leave for her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב כהנא's answer: why do we need to leave a separate pair just for the daughter?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mother stays home because her daughter is there. By the same logic, the daughter should stay because her mother is there. If so, there is no need for an extra brood for the daughter.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is different?', asking why two cases are treated differently

phrases.english: What is different about her mother?
That she is attached to her daughter
and to the mate that we leave for her;
she too
should be attached to her mother
and to the mate that we leave for her!

steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's claim that a separate pair is needed for the daughter
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The mother's bond to her daughter keeps her home, so the daughter's bond to her mother should keep her home too.

steps.title: A mother is attached to her daughter, but not the other way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the bond only goes one way: a mother clings to her daughter, but a daughter doesn't cling to her mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: A mother is attached to her daughter; a daughter is not attached to her mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by saying the attachment is not equal in both directions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the daughter doesn't feel tied to her mother, her mother being there won't keep her home. She needs her own young left with her. So רב כהנא's two pairs both make sense.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's two broods: one keeps the mother dove (who clings to her young), and one keeps the daughter (who only clings to her own young, not to her mother). The משנה mentions just the daughter's pair.

phrases.english: A mother is attached to her daughter,
a daughter is not attached to her mother.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual distinction between the two cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Mother and daughter are equally attached to each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the mother is attached to her daughter; the daughter needs her own brood to stay.

steps.title: How are the bees made sterile?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's beehive ruling and asks how the bees are made sterile.
steps.simpleTranslation: The produce of a beehive: he takes three swarms and makes them sterile. With what does he make them sterile?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and asks a practical question: how is the sterilizing done?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the bees are made sterile after three swarms but doesn't say how. This sets up the answers in the next two steps.

phrases.english: The produce of a beehive:
he takes three swarms, and makes them sterile.
With what does he make them sterile?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The method used to stop the bees from making new swarms.

steps.title: שמואל: with mustard
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: the bees are made sterile with mustard.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: with mustard.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question: mustard is what stops the bees from swarming.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Feeding the bees mustard stops them from making new swarms, so they make honey for the seller instead. שמואל doesn't explain how it works; the next step does.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
With mustard.

steps.title: In ארץ ישראל: the mustard works indirectly, through the honey
steps.stepSummary: The scholars of ארץ ישראל, quoting רבי יוסי בר חנינא, say mustard itself doesn't sterilize. It burns the bees' mouths, so they eat their own honey, and that stops the swarming.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say in ארץ ישראל in the name of רבי יוסי בר חנינא: it isn't the mustard that sterilizes them. Since their mouths sting, they turn back and eat their honey.
steps.whatsHappening: Another teaching explains how the mustard works: it does the job indirectly, not by itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mustard is sharp, so the bees' mouths burn. To soothe them, they eat lots of their own honey. Eating that honey is what stops them from making new swarms.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying mustard isn't used. Both agree the bees are fed mustard; ארץ ישראל only explains that the honey they eat afterward is what does the sterilizing.

phrases.english: They say in the West
in the name of Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina:
It is not the mustard that makes them sterile;
rather, because their mouths sting,
they turn back and eat their own honey.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי בְּמַעְרְבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how שמואל's mustard works and corrects the idea that mustard sterilizes directly.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Mustard stings the bees' mouths, so they eat their own honey, and that stops them from swarming.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The bees are given mustard; it works indirectly by making them eat their own honey.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: 'מסרס' means skipping every other swarm
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the משנה's word for 'sterilizing' really means the buyer takes his three swarms by skipping.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: He takes three swarms by skipping.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a completely different reading of the משנה's word 'מסרס'. He says it is not about sterilizing bees at all, but about skipping swarms.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 7-8 understood 'מסרס' as making the bees sterile. רבי יוחנן reads the same root as 'mixing up the order.' The buyer takes one swarm, skips the next, and so on, until he has three. The seller keeps the skipped swarms.

keyTerms.meaning: Swarms of bees that leave the hive to start a new colony
By skipping, taking them out of order (here: every other swarm)

steps.confusionAlert: Same word, two meanings. In steps 7-8 the word meant 'sterilizing.' For רבי יוחנן it means 'skipping.' Don't mix the two readings together.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says:
He takes three swarms, by skipping.
phrases.notes: He means: first swarm to the buyer, second to the seller, third to the buyer, and so on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different meaning of 'מסרס' instead of the sterilizing explanation of steps 7-8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does 'מסרס' in the משנה mean?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It means the buyer takes his three swarms by skipping every other one.

steps.title: A ברייתא: three swarms in a row, then alternate
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the buyer takes the first three swarms one after another, and after that takes one and leaves one.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught in a ברייתא: He takes three swarms one after the other. From then on, he takes one and leaves one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives yet another way to split the swarms between buyer and seller.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רבי יוחנן, the ברייתא gives the buyer the first three swarms straight, with no skipping. Only after those three does the alternating begin: one to the buyer, one to the seller.

keyTerms.meaning: It is taught in a ברייתא (a teaching of the תנאים not in the משנה)
One after the other, in a row
Takes one and leaves one, alternating

steps.whatToRemember: Three ways to read the swarm rule: sterilize the bees (שמואל / ארץ ישראל), skip every other swarm (רבי יוחנן), or take three in a row and then alternate (the ברייתא).

phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: נוֹטֵל שְׁלֹשָׁה נְחִילִין בָּזֶה אַחַר זֶה,
phrases.english: He takes three swarms one after the other,
from here onward,
he takes one and leaves one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a ברייתא with a different division of the swarms than רבי יוחנן's.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How exactly does the buyer take his swarms?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first three in a row, then alternating one for him and one for the seller.

steps.title: רב כהנא: Honey in a hive is always food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about leaving two honeycombs, and רב כהנא rules that honey in a beehive never loses its status as food.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: Honeycombs: he leaves two combs, etc. רב כהנא said: Honey in a beehive never stops being considered food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה, about honeycombs. רב כהנא makes a statement about honey's status as food for the laws of טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food can become טמא only if it counts as food. רב כהנא says honey sitting in the hive always counts as food, no matter what.

keyTerms.meaning: Does not leave the status of food

phrases.aramaic: חַלּוֹת דְּבַשׁ – מַנִּיחַ שְׁתֵּי חַלּוֹת וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Honeycombs: he leaves two combs, etc.
Rav Kahana said:
Honey in a beehive
never leaves the status of food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: moves from the swarms to the honeycombs line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Honey in a beehive is always considered food.

steps.title: Inference: Honey needs no intention to count as food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that רב כהנא holds honey does not need מחשבה, a plan to eat it, to count as food.
steps.simpleTranslation: So it seems רב כהנא holds that no intention is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion about what רב כהנא must believe. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some things only count as food for טומאה if a person plans to eat them (מחשבה). Because רב כהנא said honey is 'always' food, he must hold that honey needs no such plan.

keyTerms.meaning: Intention, a person's plan to use something as food

phrases.english: Apparently, he holds
it does not require intention.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out the underlying position behind רב כהנא's statement.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב כהנא holds that honey counts as food without any intention.

steps.title: Challenge: A ברייתא says hive honey is neither food nor liquid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב כהנא from a ברייתא that says honey in a hive is neither food nor liquid.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: Honey in a beehive is neither food nor drink!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב כהנא with a ברייתא that seems to say the exact opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא said honey in a hive is always food. The ברייתא says it is not food at all, and not a liquid either. So it cannot become טמא, which directly contradicts him.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Honey in a beehive
is neither food nor liquid!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב כהנא's ruling from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's ruling that honey in a hive is always food
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly says honey in a hive is not food, a direct contradiction.

steps.title: אביי: The ברייתא means only the two combs left for the bees
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the ברייתא is talking only about the two honeycombs left in the hive for the bees.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The ברייתא is needed only for those two combs.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends רב כהנא by narrowing the ברייתא to a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two combs from our משנה are left for the bees to eat, not for people. Those combs are not food. All other honey in the hive is still food, just as רב כהנא said.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for (the case of)
For those two combs (left for the bees)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the classic move of limiting a source to a narrow case, so two statements that seemed to clash can both be true.

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: לָא צְרִיכָא אֶלָּא לְאוֹתָן שְׁתֵּי חַלּוֹת.
phrases.english: It is needed only for those two combs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13 by limiting the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say all honey in a hive is not food.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the two combs set aside for the bees are not food. All other hive honey is food.

steps.title: רבא: The ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבא begins a different answer: the ברייתא follows the opinion of רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is the opinion of רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a second way to answer the challenge. He says the ברייתא is the view of one תנא, רבי אליעזר. The explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of narrowing the ברייתא like אביי, רבא says it follows רבי אליעזר's view. So רב כהנא simply holds like the other opinion. The details of רבי אליעזר's view come next.

phrases.english: Rava said:
It is the opinion of Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 13, different from אביי's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the source to a single תנא's opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to be the accepted rule against רב כהנא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא reflects רבי אליעזר's view, so רב כהנא can hold the other view.
